citations.claim: At first violating step 19 pole angle -0.857 rad exceeds 0.8 limit, cart at x=0.85
System energy inflated to ~20.46 by controller work driven by noisy feedback
One step before violation pole already at -0.746 rad and diverging with high velocity
Mid-run at step 15 pole already at -0.45 rad with cart accelerating, showing unstable feedback loop

counterfactual.change: Set sensor_noise from 0.0196 to 0, keeping all other fields identical; failure disappears, confirming noisy angle measurement drives destabilizing feedback.

explanation: Seeded sensor noise (~0.02 max) corrupts pole-angle measurement fed to fixed state-feedback controller. With initial offset theta=0.05 and v=0.23, noisy feedback causes overcorrection (controller forces ~22-26N), pumping energy (E ~20.5 vs E0~1.75) and driving cart velocity to ~5.8 m/s and omega to -6.7 rad/s. Pole diverges monotonically from step 10 (-0.13 rad) to step 15 (-0.45 rad) to step 18 (-0.75 rad) to step 19 (-0.857 rad), violating pole_upright. Removing noise alone stabilizes the run.
vision_note: The pole leans increasingly to the left through steps 16 to 18 while the cart stays near center. At step 19 the pole tip turns red at a large lean angle, marking the upright violation.
